response: {"title":"Deadline-aware test timeout","intervention":"Run the highest-risk affected test group first with a timeout equal to the smaller of twice its observed or estimated runtime and half the remaining deadline, then spend the residual verification time only on tests of modules that exchange data with the changed code.","claim":"Compared with no appended instruction, this timeout-bounded prioritization will raise hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses on multi-module Python tasks.","mechanism":"The rule puts the most failure-prone affected behavior first, caps exposure to hangs or unexpectedly slow suites, and targets remaining effort at cross-module data contracts where integration errors concentrate.","assumptions":["The agent can rank one affected test group as highest risk.","Test duration can be observed or estimated well enough to set a useful timeout.","Modules exchanging data define a meaningful integration-risk set."],"risks":["Timeout termination may discard a test that was about to reveal a failure.","Risk ranking can select an expensive low-yield group.","Shared state or side effects may make a timed-out run contaminate later tests.","Non-data interactions such as timing or configuration may be omitted."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched multi-module Python tasks to the appended instruction or no-instruction control under identical fixed deadlines, models, tools, and hidden tests.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"The treatment arm has higher pass_rate with deadline-miss frequency no higher than control; wall_time and turns are secondary efficiency checks."},"single_shot_ordinal":9}
